data.name: Aqsaa
data.long_meaning: Aqsaa is derived from the Arabic word 'Aqsa' which means 'The Near One'. It is a name given to the mosque in Jerusalem, Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa, which is believed to be the second holiest site in Islam, after the Kaaba in Mecca.
data.spiritual_meaning: Aqsaa is a name that symbolizes closeness to Allah and protection from harm. It is also believed to represent the power of travel and exploration, as the mosque in Jerusalem is a place of pilgrimage for Muslims.
data.numerology_meaning: Aqsaa is a name with a 6 life path number, which represents harmony, love, and balance. It suggests that Aqsaa is a nurturing and caring individual who values stability and security.

in_arabic.name: أقصى
in_arabic.meaning: الأبعد أو الأقصى في المسافة أو الدرجة
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم علم مؤنث من أصل عربي، يعني الأبعد أو الأقصى في المسافة أو الدرجة. وقد ورد في القرآن الكريم في سورة الإسراء: 'ولقد جعلنا بعضكم لبعض فتنة أتقون' ثم قال: 'وكان عنهم ما يقدمون له من العمل في الحياة الدنيا أبعد مما كانوا يعملون' (الإسراء: 60). ويشير إلى المكانة الرفيعة أو الغاية القصوى.

in_urdu.name: اقصی
in_urdu.meaning: سب سے دور یا انتہائی حد تک
in_urdu.long_meaning: عربی मूल کا علم مؤنث نام، جس کا مطلب ہے سب سے دور یا انتہائی حد تک۔ عربی جڑوں سے ماخوذ، 'قصی' کا مطلب ہے دور یا بعید۔ اسلامی تقالید میں، یہ نام قرآن مجید میں سورة الإسراء میں ذکر کیا گیا ہے، جو اللہ کی قدرت اور انسانی زندگی کے تجربات کی گہرائیوں کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: अक्सा
in_hindi.meaning: सबसे दूर या चरम सीमा तक
in_hindi.long_meaning: अरबी मूल का एक स्त्रीलिंग नाम, जिसका अर्थ होता है सबसे दूर या चरम सीमा तक। इसकी जड़ें अरबी भाषा में हैं, जहां 'अक्सा' का अर्थ होता है दूर या अधिकतम। इस्लामी परंपरा में, यह नाम कुरआन में सूरतुल-इसरा में आता है, जो अल्लाह की शक्ति और मानव जीवन के अनुभवों की गहराई को दर्शाता है।

in_english.name: Aqsaa
in_english.long_meaning: A feminine given name of Arabic origin, meaning farthest or highest degree. Etymologically derived from the Arabic root 'q-s-y', which connotes distance or extremity. Referenced in the Quran (Surah Al-Isra, verse 60), signifying elevated status or ultimate limits. Symbolizes spiritual aspirations and the pursuit of excellence.

data.cultural_impact: Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa in Jerusalem is a significant site in Islamic history, as it is where multiple Islamic prophets, including Prophet Ibrahim and Prophet Ismail, are believed to have worshipped. The site holds great importance to the Islamic community, as it is seen as a symbol of their connection to the Holy Land and the Jewish-Christian tradition.
data.spiritual_significance: Al-Masjid Al-Aqsa represents the spiritual link between Muslims and their past, as it is believed that the Prophet Muhammad visited the site during his night journey (Isra and Mi'raj) in the 7th century CE. It is a place of worship and pilgrimage, offering spiritual refuge and connection to God for Muslims around the world. The name 'Aqsa' emphasizes this spiritual connection, as it means 'The Near One', symbolizing the closeness and nearness of God.
